clue.text: Virtually ready IT company that's been trashed

indicators.note: the IT company is what has been put into the rubbish, so it sits inside the word for where trash goes

parts.note: something trashed is binned, put in the BIN

explanation.surface: A tech firm has gone under and been scrapped, almost ready for the rubbish heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash, and 'Virtually' points to money that exists only online.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptocurrency is money existing only in digital form, and ready is slang for cash.

clue.text: St. Moritz sport with good climbing stick

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means a letter moves upward to the top of the word

parts.note: the luge, a small toboggan raced at the Swiss resort of St Moritz

explanation.surface: A winter-sport racer at St Moritz is climbing with a good stick, like a ski pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The G already in the sledging word stands for 'good' and is lifted from third place to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick things is to fix them with adhesive, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Combo of Gangnam Style trios is disturbed

indicators.note: trios are runs of three letters, so only three letters survive from inside the first word
a combination joins on a second three-letter run, the opening of the other word, its tail dropped

explanation.surface: A mash-up of the Gangnam Style dance-trio routines is unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: Gangnam Style was a 2012 K-pop hit; 'trios' keeps three letters of GANGNAM (ANG), and 'Combo of' adds three from STYLE (STY).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of teenage anxiety and unease can be called disturbed, a near synonym.

clue.text: Hard stuff from raucous closet drama that's tad off

indicators.note: a raucous scene is disorderly, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled
the letters of the little word tad go off, removed from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something strong comes out of a noisy, slightly off-key coming-out play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raucous' scrambles CLOSET DRAMA and 'off' takes T, A, D out of the pool, leaving CLOSERMA to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names a hardened patch of skin or tissue, literally hard stuff.

clue.text: Transfer male silver medallists on time

parts.note: men who came second are second men

explanation.surface: Move the men who won silver on to the next event in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary posting of an employee to another department or organisation is a transfer.

clue.text: Book mobile operator to ring unknown German place

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so the network name surrounds the unknown

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
Z is a mathematical unknown
Kiel is a port city in northern Germany

explanation.surface: Book a mobile network engineer to phone some mystery town in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a UK mobile phone network; it rings Z, one of the algebraic unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: This prophet gives his name to a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Training with Zulu for record? It might get one down

indicators.note: putting the Zulu letter in place of another word, joined by with
for marks what is swapped out, the word for a record

parts.note: discipline is training in obedience or method
a disc is a gramophone record
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Coaching with a Zulu warrior for a record attempt might bring someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... for' swaps DISC out of DISCIPLINE and Z in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable ride carries a person from a high point down to the ground, so it gets them down.

clue.text: Busy music section initially gets singer cross

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word section

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A lively passage of music at first makes the vocalist angry.
explanation.walkthrough: A zo (also dzo) is a Himalayan yak-cow hybrid, a crossword favourite for 'cross'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lively, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, so busy music.

clue.text: £25, say, for post that came up?

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to express is to say

explanation.surface: Twenty-five pounds, perhaps, for a mail delivery that has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pony' is British slang for £25. The question mark points to riders: the mail 'came up' on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier mail service of 1860 carried letters by relays of riders on horseback.

clue.text: Catching former tax fiddle, expert means to consult files

indicators.note: the expert word catches the rest, holding it between its first and last letters

parts.note: an ace is an expert
cess is an old word for a tax or levy
cod means fake or a hoax, a fiddle

explanation.surface: An expert catches someone fiddling old taxes and opens up the files.
explanation.definitionFit: A password or PIN is the means by which you get into computer files.

clue.text: Treed so densely and so darkly (except for the odd bits)

indicators.note: dropping every odd-numbered letter leaves only the even ones of the phrase so darkly

explanation.surface: A wood so thickly planted and so shadowy, apart from a few patches.
explanation.definitionFit: Land full of oak trees is densely wooded with one kind of tree.

clue.text: Why some blokes might hate Florence or Paris?

definitions.text: Why some blokes might hate Florence or Paris?

parts.words: Why some blokes might hate Florence or Paris?
parts.note: Florence and Paris look like cities but are women's names, so hating them is hating women

explanation.surface: Some men seem to dislike certain Italian or French cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence and Paris pose as cities but are read as women's first names (Florence Nightingale, Paris Hilton).
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred of women is the reason some men would hate women named Florence or Paris.

clue.text: What's 'clammy' when it's served up by natives?

definitions.text: What's 'clammy' when it's served up by natives?

parts.note: natives are oysters, especially those from Whitstable or Colchester; the setter's plural reads as the dish's first word

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: clammy means damp, wet
it's contracts to the letter S after the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Asks what dish is clammy when native shellfish are served in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natives' is a British term for farmed oysters. 'served up' turns WET + S into STEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of shellfish simmered in milk is literally clammy, made with bivalve shellfish.

clue.text: Many British thrown out of club

indicators.note: the abbreviation for British is ejected from the club's name

parts.note: Boodle's is a gentlemen's club in St James's, London

explanation.surface: Plenty of Britons got expelled from the club.
explanation.walkthrough: Boodle's is an old gentlemen's club in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots or loads is the informal sense, a great many.

clue.text: Bit in papers after a small dose of drug reportedly caused death

indicators.note: after places the papers piece behind the earlier pieces
reportedly means the word is as heard, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a fix is an addict's dose

indicators.note: in puts the past tense of bite inside the papers

parts.note: ID means identity papers
bit as past tense of bite gives ate

explanation.surface: A snippet in the newspapers says a small dose of drug caused a death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' is the past tense of bite, not a small piece; ID is the usual crossword shorthand for identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate someone kills them, so the verb past tense means caused death.

clue.text: Deciding set stuck at 6-6?

parts.note: a panel of twelve jurors split evenly cannot reach a verdict, though the tennis image of a final set at six games all is the decoy

explanation.surface: A tennis match's final set is level at six games each.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis reading of 'Deciding set' is the decoy: the set of people deciding is twelve jurors split down the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel of twelve that cannot agree on a verdict is deadlocked, here at six votes each.

clue.text: Grief, I'm content to clear a cheque!

indicators.note: content means what is held inside, the letters within the words clear a cheque

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief at a cheque finally clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grief' here is British slang for nagging or hassle, as in 'stop giving me grief'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, constant complaining or nagging is a pain in the ear, synonym for grief.

clue.text: Firm to make hole in beer bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the beer word encloses the other piece

parts.note: ale is a beer
to dent something is to make a hollow in it

explanation.surface: A company sets about damaging beer bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta cooked so it still offers some bite is firm to the tooth.

clue.text: Roughly snubbed sci-fi author's grot

parts.note: CA abbreviates circa, roughly

indicators.note: snubbed suggests cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Jules Verne, French pioneer of science fiction

explanation.surface: A rough brush-off for the science-fiction writer's grotto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grot' is a poetic word for grotto, not British slang for grime.
explanation.definitionFit: A grot is a poetic grotto, and a large underground cave is much the same.

clue.text: Adapt to new life on bench

parts.note: re means on or about
a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Getting used to a fresh start while sitting on a bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle again somewhere new is to adapt to a fresh home and way of living.

clue.text: Oiled solitary lock below lid on safe

indicators.note: in a down entry, below puts the hair piece under the top letter
the lid is the top, so the first letter of safe

parts.note: a quiff is a single lock of hair brushed up

explanation.surface: A greased lone lock of hair sits under the cap on a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oiled' is slang for drunk, not greased.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly drunk, tipsy, matches oiled in its slang sense of intoxicated.

clue.text: Female hacks missing English bar?

indicators.note: missing means the English abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: hacks are riding horses, and female horses are mares

explanation.surface: Women journalists who aren't English get kept out of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' looks like journalists, but they are horses here.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of chocolate is famously sold as a bar, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Plant unusual feature when leader's gone after kid

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled piece behind the teasing word

parts.note: to kid is to josh, tease

indicators.note: unusual means changed from its normal form, so the letters are rearranged
the leader is the first letter of feature, dropped

explanation.surface: An odd feature of a plant once its top has gone after a young goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leader's gone' takes F from FEATURE, leaving EATURE, which 'unusual' rearranges into UATREE.
explanation.definitionFit: This yucca of the American south-west desert is a plant, a species of tree-like shrub.

clue.text: Give lift to wrong toddler

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word reads it upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Pick up a small child who has gone the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal wrong; reading it upward gives TROT, an old word for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is an old word for a toddling infant, a small child just able to walk.

clue.text: Frenchman? With no map, he's suffering hyperthermia

indicators.note: suffering means in distress, so the letters are scrambled
with no means the letters of the following words are removed from the pool

parts.note: he's gives the two letters of he, the apostrophe-s being a link

explanation.surface: A Frenchman without a map is overheating badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' takes M, A, P, H, E out of HYPERTHERMIA and 'suffering' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French male first name, so one bearer is a Frenchman, as with footballer Henry.

clue.text: Okay to replace centre with forward? That's pants!

indicators.note: the middle letter of the agreement word is swapped for the other piece

parts.note: yes is an okay, an agreement
front means the forward part

explanation.surface: A football tactic swapping a centre-half for a striker is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British for underpants and slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's briefs with an inverted-Y-shaped seam are underpants, called pants in British English.
